text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Budget spending within 1996 limits, says Serbian government.
- Visiting Cypriot Foreign Minister Alecos Michaelides signs bilateral cooperation agreements, meets Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Yugoslav Interior Minister Vukasin Jokanovic visits Bonn to discuss modalities on return of emigrants.
- Indicators show that estimates on further stabilisation of the market and prices are realistic, says Dragan Tomic, Serbian minister coordinator.
- Eighty eight Yugoslav banks register total loss of over 100 million dinars in first half of the year.
- Yugoslavia cannot return to international institutions with unstable exchange rate and high inflation, say central bank vice-governors Ratko Banovic and Zarko Trbojevic.
- Yugoslav United Left (JUL) launches election campaign in Novi Sad which will end on October 31 in Belgrade.
- Dragoslav Avramovic, former Yugoslav central Bank governor, withdraws as leader of opposition coalition Zajedno due to health reasons.
- Ownership transformation is key to lasting stabilisation of the economy, says President of the Serbian trade union Tomislav Banovic.
- Serbian taxi drivers end strike after reaching agreement with government.

- Sir Arthur Watts, internatinal mediator for economic succession of the former Yugoslavia arrived in Belgrade Wendesday to prepare with the Yugoslav team for the multilateral meeting scheduled for October 14 and 15 in Brussels.

- Negotiations with EU over sale of livestock and meat on the European market expected to end by end of year and exports to start next year, says secretary for foreign ecnomic relations in the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Milan Njegomir.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic to visit Zimbabwe, Guinea, Tanzania and Ghana next week.
